questions.q: What does `"1" == 1` evaluate to, and why?
options: false, because the types don't match
true, because == coerces the string to a number before comparing
It throws an error
undefined
questions.explain: == performs type coercion first, converting "1" to the number 1, so the comparison becomes 1 == 1, which is true.

questions.q: Why does ServiceNow scripting style strongly favor === over ==?
options: === runs noticeably faster on the platform
== is deprecated and no longer works
=== avoids silent, surprising type coercion by checking type and value together
There is no actual difference between them
questions.explain: === never converts types before comparing, which avoids bugs like comparing a form field's string value against a number without realizing it.

questions.q: Given `var isAssigned = false;`, what does `isAssigned && doSomething()` do?
options: It always calls doSomething() first, then checks isAssigned
It throws an error because isAssigned is false
It never calls doSomething() at all, because && short-circuits once the left side is false
It calls doSomething() and ignores isAssigned entirely
questions.explain: && short-circuits: once the left operand is false, the overall result is already false, so the right side is never evaluated.
